data.name: Sadruddin
data.gender_notes: Sadruddin is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Sadruddin is derived from the Arabic words ‘Sadr’ meaning ‘servant’ or ‘helper’ and ‘uddin’ meaning ‘faith’ or ‘god’. The name Sadruddin means ‘servant of God’ or ‘helper of the faith’. The name Sadruddin carries the meaning “Servant of God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Sadruddin usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Sadruddin is a powerful reminder of one's spiritual duties and responsibilities towards God and the community. It encourages one to be a servant and helper of the faith, and to use one's talents and abilities to serve and uplift others.
data.etymology: Sadruddin belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sadruddin total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sadruddin carries a rich historical significance in Islamic culture. It is a name borne by renowned scholars, rulers, and saints throughout Islamic history. One of the most famous bearers of this name is Sadruddin Ajam-i-Shahid, the Turkmen general who led the Islamic military campaigns against the Crusaders in the 12th century. His victories at the Battles of Ascalon and Montgisard are still celebrated in Islamic tradition as major turning points in the struggle against the Crusaders.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sadruddin holds deep spiritual significance for Muslims. It is a constant reminder of the essential belief that every individual is a servant of God and that helping others, spreading knowledge, and strengthening the faith are essential duties and acts of worship. This name instills a sense of humility, service, and devotion, inspiring individuals to lead lives in accordance with Islamic values and principles.
